findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the datetime sort key, so every non-empty page on ?optimized_pagination=true raises TypeError and returns 500.
findings.evidence: The endpoint uses order_by='-datetime' and AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField. build_cursor calls key() whenever there are results. All four seats reproduced the error with `python3 -c "import math,datetime; math.floor(datetime.datetime.now())"`, which gives TypeError: must be real number. Proposed red test: as the org owner, create one audit entry and call get_success_response(org.slug, qs_params={'optimized_pagination':'true'}).
findings.reason: Four seats agree and the TypeError mechanism was reproduced. Severity is normalised to Critical because the whole opt-in path fails for any org that has audit logs.

findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. build_queryset then compares the datetime column against an integer, so follow-up pages fail or return wrong rows.
findings.evidence: value_from_cursor (paginator.py:838-843) was copied from the integer Paginator. DateTimePaginator (around line 230-241) converts the cursor to a datetime first. The raw SQL `"datetime" <= %s` compares a timestamptz to an int. This is reasoned and was not executed.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. This is a distinct cause from the get_item_key TypeError. It needs a red test on a second-page cursor.

findings.claim: The negative-offset 'advanced' branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start. Django raises ValueError, which is not a BadPaginationError, so any client cursor like 0:-5:0 returns 500.
findings.evidence: django==5.2.1 (requirements-frozen.txt:36) raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'). paginate() in api/base.py:540 only catches BadPaginationError. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets. Proposed red request: GET /api/0/organizations/{slug}/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-5:0. This is reasoned because Django was not installed.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. The fix is to reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError or remove the branch.

findings.claim: In the shared BasePaginator.get_result, a negative offset on a prev cursor (is_prev=1) is still passed straight to the queryset slice. Every subclass (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, ...) therefore returns 500 for a client cursor like 0:-5:1.
findings.evidence: The new line is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. Django refuses negative slices and only BadPaginationError is caught. Proposed red test: get_error_response(org.slug, qs_params={'cursor':'0:-5:1'}, status_code=400) returns 500. Ponytail notes the old code also sliced the raw offset, so this may already exist on the base.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Severity is normalised to Important because it is a client-triggerable 500 on every paginated endpoint. It may already exist on the base; the red test on the pinned code still applies.

findings.claim: For non-prev cursors the negative offset is clamped to 0 for the slice, but the unclamped cursor.offset is still used later (line 192 and build_cursor). This produces inconsistent next/prev cursors.
findings.evidence: open-code-review: the clamp hides the negative offset but leaves cursor.offset negative when build_cursor uses it. superpowers: line 192 still compares against the unclamped offset. This is reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not reported and not fixed. Unverified.

findings.claim: The change to the shared BasePaginator is unscoped. It alters every subclass only to serve the new audit-log paginator, adds no value, and should be reverted to the plain offset slice.
findings.evidence: mattpocock: every BasePaginator subclass is changed and test_paginator.py has no tests for it. ponytail: extra code in shared logic that buys nothing; revert to `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])`.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not reported and not fixed.

findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat, so it is not reported and not fixed.

findings.evidence: superpowers calls this a stated intent to bypass pagination bounds that only fails because Django refuses negative slices. open-code-review says the permissions claim is irrelevant to an offset. mattpocock found no actual data-exposure path for the same reason.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not reported and not fixed. The seat reports show no exposure path, since Django blocks the slice. Unverified.

findings.claim: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every request. When member is None (a non-member caller without the raw superuser flag, such as a legacy ApiKey or org token whose request.user is AnonymousUser), it raises AttributeError and returns 500, even without optimized_pagination.
findings.evidence: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed RpcOrganizationMember | None (organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). OrganizationPermission lets non-members in via is_active_superuser and request.auth paths. Proposed red test: authenticate with an ApiKey with scope_list=['org:write'], GET the endpoint, and expect 200. This is reasoned.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Severity is normalised to Critical because open-code-review and superpowers show it fires on the default path, which regresses the existing audit-log listing.

findings.claim: span-buf:s:* keys change from SET to ZSET with no migration, prefix bump or dual-read. During a rolling deploy, old and new consumers hit WRONGTYPE on each other's keys. p.execute() raises, which can crash-loop the process and flush consumers for up to redis_ttl (3600s) and lose spans buffered in old keys.
findings.evidence: New code runs zadd/zcard/zunionstore/zscan (add-buffer.lua:46,52; buffer.py:197,434) on keys that old pods created with sadd. Old pods run scard/sscan on the new zsets. redis-py pipelines raise on the first error. This is reasoned and nothing was run against Redis.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. A red test is feasible by pre-seeding a SET-type key in the test Redis and running process_spans.

findings.claim: The max_segment_spans parameter (default 1001) is still accepted and stored but never read. Its only reader was removed and the cap is now a hard-coded 1000 in add-buffer.lua, so tuning it silently does nothing and the default disagrees with the real limit.
findings.evidence: buffer.py:150,158 still store it. The old check at buffer.py:446 was removed. add-buffer.lua:62-63 uses the literal 1000. open-code-review: grep finds no other reader.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Normalised to Minor. Either delete the parameter or pass it to the script as ARGV.
